mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals accommodative monetary policy supporting the housing sector, which boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.4 percentage points in a single month, coupled with a concurrent drop in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 150,000, signals a sudden labor market shock, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp AND PAYEMS < 150000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.7% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
